root_idea.summary: No independent root-level semantic principle is established by the supplied evidence. The directly attested lexical center is a balance or weighing instrument, with extensions to particular balance types and standards.
root_idea.development: The lexical discussion records a proposed association with قِسْط meaning justice, alongside a competing account that the word is an Arabicized Greek term. Neither account establishes a broader productive root development here.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized dictionary headword قِسْطَاس.

senses.definition: A balance or instrument for weighing.
senses.usage_conditions: In the supplied Quranic occurrences, used with بِـ in the expression بِالْقِسْطَاسِ, in instructions concerning weighing and measurement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The most even and just kind of balance; also something just, whatever its kind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied in Classical Arabic beyond the physical weighing instrument to a thing characterized as just.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A steelyard; also the iron or beam of a steelyard or balance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote the whole instrument or a specified structural part such as its iron or beam.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A public standard of weights or measures.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Denotes a recognized standard used for weighing or measurement, distinct from merely naming a balance instrument.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The unit supplies the Quran-attested weighing-instrument sense and the Classical extensions to justness, steelyards or their parts, and public measurement standards.

cautions: The lexical evidence records both قُسْطَاس and قِسْطَاس, as well as an orthographic variant قصطاس; the public headword follows the QAC vocalization قِسْطَاس. Its etymology is reported both as related to قِسْط meaning justice and as an Arabicized Greek term.
